- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.6) and price is trending up, model tends to overestimate near-term peaks; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.2) and price is trending down, model often underestimates the drop; increase forecast low by 5–10%.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative; add 2–3% bias upward for such cases.
- After sharp price spikes (≥10% from prior 7-day high), model overreacts and forecasts overshoot; cap forecast at 10% above prior peak.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias in 30-day forecasts when sentiment is volatile; adjust by adding 1–2% lagged 14-day average to forecast.
- When sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 0.0–0.2) over 5+ days, model underestimates true price; apply 3–5% upward bias to forecast.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 7 days show strong downward momentum, model often fails to capture rebound; add 1–3% upward bias to forecast if sentiment turns positive within next 3 days.
